I will keep my main land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is what I know best, it fits my well irrigation, and it gives my family steady grain. I do not have a big household, and some family labor goes off-farm, so I will keep the plan practical and not too labor-heavy. I will put most of my 10.1 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton because I already grow it and I want some cash income as well. I will use improved seed for wheat, hybrid seed for maize, and improved cotton seed, because I want stable emergence and better yield. I will fertilize at a medium level, not too high, because I want to control cost. Since I have well irrigation, I will irrigate wheat more than maize and cotton, because wheat in my area depends more on timely water. I will use rotary tillage because it is faster and suits my labor situation. I will spray pesticides only as much as needed to keep insects, weeds, and disease under control, because too many sprays cost money and time.
